messages:
karim: Heads up — starting bring-up for a new embeddings candidate 'stitch-bench-lite' (6B). Planning fp16 baseline + int8 quant probes, quick smoke and clustering checks.
laura: Nice. Can you include recall@k on the wiki holdout and a UMAP + silhouette sanity snapshot? :eyes:
sam: Also worth checking short-query behavior and multilingual subsets. Those often show the worst regressions.
karim: Ran initial pass this morning. Quick numbers (wiki holdout): fp16 recall@10 = 0.82, int8 (per-tensor) = 0.79. Silhouette fp16 = 0.41, int8 = 0.38. Short-queries (<20 tokens) int8 recall@10 = 0.68 vs fp16 0.71. Uploaded artifacts to: gs://redwood-evals/stitchbench/2026-03-22/
jordana: Those deltas look small but nontrivial. Can you paste the quant command + config so infra can reproduce?
karim: Sure — command I used:
```bash
python quantize.py --model stitch-bench-lite --method per_tensor --bits 8 --calib-samples 2048 --out-dir /tmp/stitch_int8
# config snippet:
# {"quant":{"method":"per_tensor","sym":true,"clip_method":"mse"},"dtype":"int8"}
```
laura: Thanks. Also try per-channel quant; historically that regains quality for embeddings. And check cosine vs dot product retrieval — we normalize downstream sometimes.
karim: Did both quick checks. Per-channel int8: recall@10 = 0.80 (so only -0.02 vs fp16), binary size +12%. Cosine-normalized retrieval gives +0.02 recall across the board vs raw dot. Multilang (fr/es) showed no material regressions.
sam: Any nondeterminism or weird failure modes at inference — e.g., microbatching vs single request?
karim: Microbatch tests (batch=1,4,8) — recall stable within ±0.005; latency improved ~2.3x at batch=8. No nondeterminism beyond FP noise. KV-cache path behaves same for streaming vs non-streaming.
jordana: If we consider promoting int8, we should add regression alerts in the eval harness: recall@1/10, silhouette, mean cosine, per-lang. I can author the rollout checklist. @laura does that capture your ask?
laura: Yep. Also add a long-tail holdout sweep (k up to 100) and hard-negative stress tests. If finance/legal categories show centroid drift we need a deeper look. :mag_right:
karim: Quick notes from UMAPs I pushed — clusters preserved overall. Saw a small centroid drift on the finance category (~0.04 mean cosine shift) with per-tensor int8, mitigated by per-channel. Artifacts: UMAP/*.png, recall_tables/*.csv in the GS path.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy for 'stitch-bench-lite:int8-per-channel' scheduled: 2026-03-23 18:00 UTC — notify #eng-ml on start.
jordana: I'll own the rollout doc + post-deploy checks. Plan: canary 5% queries, run live recall probe vs control, rollback if recall@10 drop > 0.01 on daily aggregate or any category >0.03.
sam: Sounds good. After canary, let's run the full multilingual K=1..100 sweep and a hard-negatives pass.
laura: TL;DR for release notes: per-channel int8 is promising (recall@10 -0.02 vs fp16) with ~12% binary growth; recommend enabling L2-normalize in pipeline to regain +0.02. Add regression gates in eval harness. :thumbsup:
karim: Uploaded a short runbook + smoke command to the GS path and linked the canary playbook in the rollout doc. Will post a final summary before the canary.
jordana: Thanks — I'll ping when the rollout doc is ready for review.
laura: Great work team.
sam: :thumbsup:
